what: The heuristic identifies customers and the depot from goal fact names, resolves their visited/location facts, and reconstructs direct and via-depot routing costs once from grounded operator names and metric operator costs. At evaluation time it finds the current location and unvisited customers, computes an MST plus directed outgoing-edge routing relaxation, and computes a nearest-neighbor constructive completion that uses visit-via-depot whenever the current route cannot fit another customer. Exact capacity, demand, and vehicle-limit fluents are optional: resource reasoning is enabled only when the relevant exact numeric names survived translation; otherwise the full routing estimate still operates without capacity constraints. The returned estimate blends the graph lower estimate with the constructive completion and assigns a large value to states that definitely exceed the aggregate vehicle capacity limit.
why: CVRP states are naturally represented by a current route endpoint, a subset of remaining customers, and a required final return to the depot. The representative instances use metric-like geometric costs, making MST/outgoing relaxations and nearest-neighbor completion inexpensive and informative. Their capacities range from very restrictive to large, so the constructive estimate benefits substantially from modeling depot route breaks when exact resource data is available. Operator-derived costs avoid unsafe dependence on folded travel-cost expressions, while optional resource handling ensures the heuristic generalizes when capacity and demand PNEs have been removed by the translator.
